Suno suit published 09/22. The v6 training-data admission is supporting detail, not a new filing. (3) Andrew Huang Short 'AI scammers are trying to use me' (09/26): the Short has no description, so the body cannot be checked, and it overlaps the 09/23 Engadget artist-page scam story. Skipped rather than published unverified. The Banoffee/Suno v6 video (Kao_5B_-a6U) had already been removed by story_dedup as the same campaign as the 10/03 Braylon Browner x Nina McNeely video. Single category 'music', so accents were rotated from the palette.

items.rationale: New Suno product feature (Albums: group, order and publish AI-made tracks as a full release), the most actionable item for creators today.
items.excerpt: Suno launches Albums: creators can group their AI-made songs into a full release, build an album draft (including from an existing playlist), organize track order and publish it on Suno.

items.rationale: Hard new figure: Sony has requested takedowns of 260,000+ AI soundalike deepfakes and calls it an uphill struggle. Shows how large the AI impersonation problem has become.
items.excerpt: Sony Music has now asked platforms to remove more than 260,000 AI deepfake tracks imitating artists like Harry Styles, Adele and Michael Jackson, telling the FT the fight against soundalike AI tracks is 'becoming an uphill struggle'.

items.rationale: New report ties the falling numbers on Spotify's flagship editorial playlists to its crackdown on fake accounts and AI slop. This is a different story from the Meta Muse integration.
items.excerpt: Follower and listener counts on Spotify's biggest editorial playlists are slipping, which a new report links to Spotify's crackdown on fake accounts and AI slop rather than waning interest.

items.rationale: Fresh artist stance with a practical line: AI-assisted lyric writing is acceptable, but AI 'artists' should not chart alongside humans.
items.excerpt: Joe Bonamassa says using Suno to write a lyric is 'not a high crime or misdemeanour' and sympathises with emerging artists using AI for an edge, but argues AI 'artists' shouldn't chart alongside humans.

items.rationale: Pope Leo XIV draws a line between human art and machine output. Music Ally places it within the music industry's AI fight. A new voice in the human-vs-AI art debate.
items.excerpt: Pope Leo XIV posts that it is 'urgent to distinguish human art from what machines produce', claiming an 'ontological difference' between art and statistically generated output; Music Ally frames it against the music industry's AI fight.
